newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Kedem in talks with Unilever.
newsitem.headline: Kedem in talks with Unilever.

text.p: Israel's Kedem Chemicals Ltd said on Tuesday it was in talks with the DiverseyLever unit of Unilever to form a joint venture in industrial cleaning and related chemicals.
"Our company is negotiations with DiverseyLever, a foreign company that is part of the Unilever concern," Kedem told the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

"The negotiations deal with the creation of a new joint venture through which the two companies will concentrate in the supply of cleaning, disinfectant and maintenance chemicals systems to the industrial and institutional sectors," Kedem said.
Kedem managing director, Eli Rikovitz, would not provide any further details about the talks or what form the joint venture would take.

Kedem, a subsidiary of Tambour Ltd, had revenues of $22 million in 1995 from household cleaning products, gardening chemicals and institutional cleaning materials. Rikovitz said the Israel market for institutional cleaning materials was $90 million to $100 million.
Kedem produces chemicals under license from Diversey, a Canadian company whose cleaning and sanitizing business were acquired by Unilever in April 1996.
